correctness.rationale: For k>=3 nonempty parts, each length-one graph edge yields exactly two antipodal extreme transportation molecules, whereas distance-two nonedges lie in convex hulls of length-one edge molecules. Two proposed oriented molecules span a face-edge iff a unit-Lipschitz exposing potential has exactly those two tight directed edges. Explicit 0/1/1/2 potentials expose common-tail or common-head pairs; consecutive-directed edges force an additional tight edge; for four distinct endpoints strict 1/2-offset potentials exist precisely when cross endpoints share a multipartite part. This proves the if-and-only-if adjacency rule. Each undirected-edge fiber consequently has exactly one neighbor orientation across intersecting part pairs, a signed 2-cover of a clique blow-up of L(K_k). Exact part-edge counts give degree N(a+b)-a²-ab-b²-1 and summed f1. For k=3 every pair of parts intersects, giving degree M-1; for k>=4 degree difference (b-c)(N-a-b-c) with positive remainder forces all sizes equal. Fiber-constant Laplacian is MI-J so eigenvalue M multiplicity>=M-1. Independently optimized all vertex-pair exposure LPs for four small cases including unbalanced tripartite and k=4; numeric tests corroborate, not prove general classifications.
